key_insight: AssayLoop learns how to choose the next CRISPR perturbations from historical screens, combining an amortized acquisition policy with LLM-based biological priors to improve adaptive hit discovery under tight budgets.
engineering_relevance: This offers a scalable sequential-design framework for experimental pipelines where candidate tests are expensive and decisions must be made online from sparse feedback.
method: Built AssayBench-Loop, a benchmark of 1,389 CRISPR screens across five phenotype categories.
Trained AssayFormer, a transformer-based policy that adapts acquisition decisions using prior experimental outcomes.
Added an adaptive handoff to LLM-derived biological priors and extended the idea into AssayLLM via task-specific post-training.
evidence_signal: On temporally held-out screens, AssayLoop achieved 5.67-fold enrichment over random and recovered 27.7% of hits after testing about 5% of the library, outperforming prior adaptive methods, standalone LLMs, and AssayFormer alone.
watch_item: Because the approach depends on historical screens and phenotype transfer, performance may degrade when training data are sparse, biased, or poorly matched to a new assay setting.
paper_title: Biology-in-the-loop: Amortized Adaptive Hit Discovery in CRISPR Screens
